sections.html:
Think of Aiken County as South Carolina's western edge, facing Georgia over the Savannah River and tied to the Augusta metro area. Aiken the city holds the county seat. North Augusta and New Ellenton are the other cities. Population reached roughly 181,515 in 2025, and the 2020 census tallied 76,923 housing units, of which 9.7% sat vacant. Owners occupy 73.2% of the lived-in homes.

A mill-village house in Graniteville, a rural parcel and a newer home near Aiken or North Augusta each attract a different buyer. Close to the Savannah River Site, in Jackson or New Ellenton for instance, expect shoppers to ask how long the site will keep its workforce.

Payment season opens September 30 and runs through January 15. Collection belongs to the county treasurer, with state Department of Revenue oversight, and receipts identify each parcel by tax map number.

Late bills climb a ladder. A 3% charge begins January 16 (or 30 days after the notice went out, whichever comes later), 7% more is stacked on if nothing is paid before February 2, and 5% more before March 17. After that the treasurer passes an execution to the delinquent collector. Mailing? The U.S. postmark settles whether you were on time.

Aiken County property tax payment calendar
StepDate or amount
Payment window opensSeptember 30
Payment window closesJanuary 15
First penalty3% from January 16 or 30 days after mailing, whichever is later
Second penalty7% added from February 2
Third penalty5% added from March 17, then execution issued

A transfer in mid-year can create a trap: the notice went to the old owner, so the new one never saw it. In that situation the penalty must be waived by the treasurer, a rule found in subsection (B) of the penalty statute.

Inherited and newly sold houses are the usual cases. Mail addressed to a person who has died, or to a seller long gone, never finds the current deed holder. Within a week of recording, request an address correction from the treasurer and file your copy of the request.

  • Send your new mailing address to the treasurer and the assessor once you close.
  • Get the balance in writing before closing.
  • Keep payment proof, with the postmark.

sections.h2: How to object to your assessment
sections.html:
Put any objection in writing to the assessor. From the mailing of an assessment notice you have 90 days to contest fair market value, special use value, the assessment ratio or the assessment as a whole.

The assessor owes you a notice for a first-time assessment or a rise of $1,000 or more. Without one, a written appeal is open all year. Timing decides the tax year it affects: before the first penalty date, it applies to the current year, and on or after that date, to the next. When the whole county is reassessed, nearly every notice has to be mailed by October 1.

Phone the Aiken County offices to learn the right form and where to hand it in.

sections.h2: Selling a house that owes back tax
sections.html:
Absolutely. Before closing, request a written payoff from the treasurer or the delinquent tax office. At the table, the title company subtracts that tax from your proceeds, leaving the buyer a clear record. Since penalties rise in steps, any payoff expires, so find out its last valid date.

Heirs frequently have to clear the tax record first, and an outdated mailing address is the common reason a bill went unseen. Cash buyers may accept a house as-is with tax owed, repairs pending or a tenant inside, though payoff and closing work the same as in any sale.

Begin with the tax map number, which the treasurer's records and receipts all use. Three questions follow: today's balance, whether this year's bill is settled, and the date each penalty would start. With an open bill, decide with the buyer how it is divided and have the title company note the split.

The buyer then sends both offices a current address. Gather the closing statement, payoff letter and any postmarked receipt in one folder, so a later question about the bill is answered from paper, not memory.

Sellers who are behind gain nothing by waiting. Each added percent increases the very balance you must clear at closing, so request the payoff early and note its good-through date to keep the number steady.

One call can rescue a closing. Learn whether the bill is open, which tax map number carries it, and whether an execution exists. Find out where the notice last went. If the address belongs to a former owner, request a penalty waiver in writing and save the answer.

Next, the assessor: was a changed-value notice sent, and on what date? Your 90 days start at that mailing, and a buyer's lender may want a copy. Planning to object? Ask for the form now, not near the deadline. Phone answers help, but written ones belong in your closing file.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited Aiken County house
sections.html:
Heirs face the tax bill before they face the buyer. Sort out who is receiving the mail first. If the notices still go to the person who died, tell the treasurer where to send them now, and ask in writing for any penalty to be waived if you never saw the notice. Then request a written payoff for every open year.

Gather the deed, the tax map number and your address change request before you list. A buyer's title company will look for open tax, and an unresolved bill slows the sale for everyone. If the house needs work, the tax can still be paid from proceeds at closing, which means you do not have to find the money up front.

Where the value on the assessor's notice looks too high, objecting does not stop the sale. File in writing, keep the mailing date of the notice, and let the title company know an objection is pending so the closing statement reflects it. Ask the assessor how an appeal filed near the January penalty date would apply, since the date decides whether it covers this year or the next.

A sale to a cash buyer drops the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which are often where a closing slips. It does not drop the tax steps. The treasurer still needs to be paid, the penalty calendar still runs, and the title company still wants a payoff letter. What you gain is a shorter list of people who can delay you.

If you are weighing offers, ask each buyer how they treat open tax, a missing notice and a changed mailing address. The answers show whether they have closed a South Carolina sale before.

faqs.q: When are Aiken County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is open from September 30 through January 15, and the 3% penalty begins January 16 or 30 days after mailing, if later.
They stack: 3%, then 7% more after February 1, then 5% more after March 16, followed by an execution from the treasurer.

faqs.q: How long do I have to object to an assessment?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the notice's mailing, in writing. The Aiken County Assessor can name the form.

faqs.q: Can the penalty be waived if I just bought the house?
faqs.a: Yes, if the notice went to the prior owner and none reached you in time. Ask the treasurer in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Aiken County house that owes back tax?
faqs.a: Yes. A written payoff from the treasurer or delinquent tax office lets the title company pay the tax from your proceeds.
